carbon_policy_signal.item: EU leaders summit (Oct 15–16) agenda includes methane rule enforcement decision; Big Oil lobbying delays risk weakening upstream emissions oversight and structural decarbonisation cost.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: Methane rule delays reduce upstream cost on Russian pipeline gas, easing TTF structural floor and lowering thermal-dispatch decarbonisation penalty — bearish to EUA long-term support and carbon-cost embedded in power merit order.

freshness_caveat: Coal data as of 2025-12-26 (293 days old) and Clean Dark as of 2025-12-31 (288 days old) are stale; do not rely on coal-power spread signals. TTF, DE Power, GB Power, Storage, EUA, and Renewables are current as of 2026-10-14/15.
risk_flags: GB Power at 96th percentile (186.36 EUR/MWh) with -8.75% daily pullback signals volatility and potential supply crunch; DE Power at 87th percentile (200 EUR/MWh) tracks upside risk.
EU Storage 14.9pp below 5-yr seasonal average at 74.02% full; refill pace through H2 will set thermal dispatch economics and power curve slope.
Slovakia PM Fico alignment with Putin escalates transit-hub leverage risk; potential disruption to Central/Southern EU gas supply carries asymmetric tail risk to power spreads.
Methane rule delays remove upstream emissions cost for Russian pipeline gas, structurally supporting TTF floor and weakening decarbonisation incentive in power merit order.

base.summary: GB premium persists; EU storage refill gradual; geopolitical tail risk priced but not shocked.

downside.summary: EU summit backs Green Deal; emergency brake stalls; methane rule re-tightened; renewables forecast above 60th percentile softens thermal call.

upside.summary: Slovakia-Russia pipeline deal signals supply cut or transit leverage; Ukraine refinery campaign lifts Brent crude; thermal call extends.

themes: GB Power extreme tightness vs EU storage deficit
Methane rule delay eases upstream cost, bearish power floor
Emergency brake on EU laws threatens Green Deal enforcement
top_drivers: GB Power at 96th percentile (186.36 EUR/MWh) driven by supply tightness and storage deficit; DE Power at 87th percentile tracks systemic thermal call.
Slovakia-Putin alignment raises pipeline leverage risk and potential supply disruption volatility to Central/Southern EU power and TTF structural support.
Methane rule delays by Big Oil remove upstream emissions cost for Russian gas, easing TTF floor and weakening decarbonisation signal in merit order.
top_takeaway: GB Power at 96th percentile (186.36 EUR/MWh) dominates; storage 14.9pp below seasonal average tilts H2 thermal risk upward; Slovakia-Russia pivot threatens pipeline leverage.

At 74.02% (14.9pp below seasonal); refill pace determines thermal call into H2 and power curve risk through winter.

watchlist.why: Sustained Ukrainian strikes tighten crude supply; higher Brent lifts crude-to-gas switching incentive in EU power stack, supporting thermal dispatch economics.
